qualification: local pinned-fixture correctness and bounded production-admission evidence; not hardware, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

kernelPatchEvidence.interpretation: The pinned Linux image registers the measured lock prefix for SMP alternatives and replaces 0xf0 with the same-length 0x3e DS prefix in the uniprocessor guest.

admission.lockedSemantics: one compare-exchange callback loop through the shared x86 atomic gate, followed by an eight-bit logical lazy-flags record
admission.patchedSemantics: one replay-safe byte read followed by a final transactional byte write, followed by the same logical lazy-flags record
admission.boundedRule: The patched non-atomic form is admissible only when the complete block starts at 0xffffffff8153a159 and contains exactly the measured five bytes, one guest instruction, and one IR statement.
admission.deferred: the same non-atomic operation at every other RIP, other byte immediates or sources, other widths, and all other memory-writing ALU forms

verification.dbtAndPCGate: 1,441 tests in 171 suites passed; the pinned PVH environment test skipped because its environment variables were absent
verification.differentialCoverage: Both f0 and 3e encodings match the interpreter across initial bytes 0x00, 0x01, 0x7f, 0x80, and 0xff, including architectural flags and high-canonical effective addresses.
verification.rollbackCoverage: An atomic callback failure and a patched-form failed read or failed write preserve the original architectural state and memory.
verification.concurrencyCoverage: Three mixed interpreter/tier-one workers perform 195 locked toggles through one physical byte and observe the expected single-copy result.
verification.negativeAdmissionCoverage: Immediate two, register-source, and word forms decline in both prefix images; the exact patched operation also declines at the adjacent RIP.

rejectedBroadAdmissionDiagnostic.failure: NX-protected init-text instruction fetch at 0xffffffff830c96ac while free_init_pages was setting init memory non-executable; the fatal exception in an interrupt reset the guest before its receipt
rejectedBroadAdmissionDiagnostic.interpretation: Matching only the decoded byte-XOR operation admitted unrelated memory-writing sites and reproduced the prior broad memory-ALU NX panic. This run is failure evidence and is not accepted as a correctness or performance result.

unmatchedFullRunComparison.interpretation: The two single full runs differ in dynamic instruction, interrupt, compilation, address-space, and trace totals. The elapsed change is reported for completeness and is not a performance claim.

interpretation: The pinned Linux kernel rewrites the measured locked XOR into a DS-prefixed non-atomic form. Tier one now handles both runtime images with their distinct atomicity contracts, while the fixture-RIP boundary avoids the correctness failure exposed by generic memory-XOR admission. The measured site disappears from the visible negative cache and the authenticated workload gate powers off cleanly. A05.2 remains open because 125,948 of 224,625 full-run tier-one attempts still declined.
limitations: The complete workload evidence contains one bounded candidate run on one local Apple M2 Pro.
The admission address is intentionally tied to the pinned kernel image and must not be generalized without separate memory-RMW qualification.
The hot-site sampler is capped and proves absence only from the retained visible list, not from every historical cache entry.
The prior and candidate full runs are unmatched dynamic executions and establish no performance delta.
The diagnostic runner marks every record releaseQualified=false; this evidence does not satisfy G1-G5.
